name: Spider-lily weapon ignition: gold glints and falling petals catch into a filament bloom with pink flame tendrils

source.title: Zedkiel, Spiderlily weapon VFX set (user reference video)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:16.0-0:19.5 (pair of gauntlets on black). 0:16.0-0:16.5: the dark unlit gauntlets each show a small gold cross-shaped filament flower; thin gold petal flecks start tumbling down and outward around them

phases.name: release
phases.what: 0:16.5-0:17.0: the filament flower grows into a full stamen burst (long curved gold strands radiating from one point), flame tufts curl up behind it like antlers, petal flecks are at their densest

phases.name: impact
phases.what: 0:17.0-0:17.5: the centre ignites to a white-gold core with a wide horizontal anamorphic streak and four-point glint; a soft magenta haze disc blooms behind the hand

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: 0:17.5-0:19.5: settled loop. Pink flame tendrils curl upward and outward in looping arcs, tiny pink sparkle motes orbit, petal flecks stop, the core breathes at about 1 Hz

layers.motion: thin elongated petal flecks, 40-60, spawn in a 1.2 m sphere, fall with gravity 2 and tumble (spin 6), life 0.8-1.2 s
layers.notes: they are stretched slivers, not dots: they read as falling petals and set the gold palette before anything glows

layers.motion: camera-facing radial filament flower, 12-16 curved strands from a centre point; scale 0.3 -> 1.0 over 0.9 s with ease-out
layers.notes: the hero silhouette of the whole set: a spider-lily stamen burst drawn as thin bright strands with dark gaps between them

layers.motion: 6-8 flame-tongue ribbons rooted behind the flower, curling up and out like antlers, noise-scrolled, life loops
layers.notes: orange at the root, pink at the tips; their upward lean gives the hand object a crown shape

layers.motion: small white-gold point, scale pop 0 -> 1.4 -> 1.0 over 0.15 s
layers.notes: very small and very bright; the size stays tiny so the strands remain readable

layers.motion: thin horizontal anamorphic streak 6x wider than the object plus a four-point star glint, flash in 2 frames then settle at 40%
layers.notes: lens-streak sells 'precious metal catching light' rather than fire

layers.motion: large soft magenta haze behind the object, opacity 0 -> 0.5 over 0.4 s, gentle 1 Hz pulse
layers.notes: low-opacity backdrop separates the gold strands from the black background

layers.motion: tiny pink motes spiralling up along looping arcs, life 0.6 s, drag 1.5
layers.notes: the looping arcs trace little heart / tendril curves that keep the idle alive

whyItLooksGood: One iconic shape (a spider-lily stamen burst of thin curved strands) is repeated on every weapon of the set, so the set reads as a family
The ignition is a 1 s ramp in clear steps: falling petals -> strand bloom -> white core with lens streak -> pink tendrils. Each step adds one new layer
Two-tone split: hard gold strands in front, soft magenta haze behind. Warm-on-pink keeps it rich without blowing out to white
Falling petal flecks stop once the bloom is lit, so the idle loop is calmer than the ignition
buildNotes: Video 0:16.0-0:19.5. Build as a self-attached aura on the caster's hand or weapon socket. Filament flower: a custom camera-facing mesh of 12-16 thin curved quads (or a canvas texture of curved strokes) on an additive plane; scale tween 0.3 -> 1 in 0.9 s. Petals: Emitter with stretched sprite, gravity 2, spin 6, drag 0.6, burst 50 in the first 0.6 s only. Flame tufts: 6-8 short ribbon meshes with a scrolling-UV + alpha-erosion shader, gradient orange -> pink along length. Core: small GlowSphere white-gold with a scale pop. Streak: a very thin wide additive quad (width 6x height) through the core. Backdrop: large GlowSphere magenta at 0.4 opacity. Exaggerate: the streak length and the strand count; keep the core tiny.

name: Spider-lily bow: filament bloom at the grip, flame crest up the limb, glinting nocked arrow

source.title: Zedkiel, Spiderlily weapon VFX set (user reference video)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:12.5-0:15.75 (bow close-up; also 0:00-0:12.5 in the set overview). 0:12.5-0:13.25: dark bow, small gold filament flower at the grip, gold flecks around it; flame crest grows up the upper limb

phases.name: release
phases.what: 0:13.25-0:13.75: the flower lights white-gold, three long flame ribbons stand up off the upper limb; a second small gold glint sits on the nocked arrow tip

phases.name: impact
phases.what: not in the video (idle showcase): use the arrow-tip glint as the projectile head and repeat the filament bloom at the target

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: 0:13.75-0:15.75: steady loop, pink haze behind the grip, faint sparkle motes, ribbon crest sways

layers.motion: filament flower on the grip, scale 0.4 -> 1, slow 10 deg/s spin
layers.notes: same stamen-burst silhouette as the rest of the set

layers.motion: 3 tall flame ribbons rooted along the upper limb, swaying with noise, length 0.8-1.2 m
layers.notes: tall S-curved ribbons make a crest like a feather plume; they lean back from the arrow direction

layers.motion: arrow with a small gold four-point glint on the tip; in flight it leaves a short pink trail
layers.notes: the glint on the tip is the only bright point on the arrow, so the eye follows it

layers.motion: soft magenta haze 1.5 m wide behind the grip, 1 Hz pulse 0.35 -> 0.5
layers.notes: backlight that separates the dark bow from the black background

layers.motion: sparse pink motes, 8/s, drift up and out, life 1 s
layers.notes: keeps the idle sparkling without adding brightness

layers.motion: short horizontal lens streak through the grip flower, 40% opacity
layers.notes: same lens language as the other weapons

whyItLooksGood: The weapon itself stays dark brown/black; only the flower, crest and arrow tip glow, so the silhouette of the bow still reads
Two bright points (grip flower, arrow tip) at different sizes create a clear focal hierarchy
Ribbons lean in one direction, giving the static weapon a sense of wind and motion
buildNotes: Video 0:12.5-0:15.75. For a targeted shot: put the filament flower (additive camera-facing strand mesh) and 3 flame ribbons (scrolling-UV alpha-erosion ribbon meshes, orange root -> pink tip) on the caster's hand for 0.75 s, then fire a small mesh-projectile arrow whose tip carries a four-point star sprite and a short pink trail-ribbon. On hit spawn a smaller copy of the filament flower at the target (scale 0 -> 1.2 in 0.12 s, fade in 0.5 s) with a gold petal burst Emitter (gravity 2, spin). Exaggerate the crest height; keep the haze faint.

phases.name: release

phases.name: impact

phases.name: aftermath

layers.motion: orb 0.35 m, inner gradient bright rim -> dim centre (fresnel), 0.7 Hz pulse
layers.notes: fresnel-bright rim, darker middle: reads as glass, not as a light bulb

layers.motion: 6 curved flame petals forming a cage around the orb, roots at the bottom, tips curling inward at the top, slow upward UV scroll
layers.notes: petals frame the orb: the cage silhouette is the staff's icon

layers.motion: small gold filament star in the orb centre, slow rotation

buildNotes: Video 0:19.5-0:23.0. As a channel: put the orb (GlowSphere with fresnel shader, pink) and 6 flame-petal ribbons (custom curved ribbon meshes, scrolling-UV + alpha erosion) on the caster's hand, then draw a thin pink beam-ribbon to the target with gold filament stars blooming along it every 0.4 s. Pink dust: Emitter gravity 0.8 from the orb downward. Exaggerate the petal curl and the fresnel rim.

name: Spider-lily scythe: blade wrapped in a long flowing flame ribbon, usable as the swing trail

source.title: Zedkiel, Spiderlily weapon VFX set (user reference video)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:23.0-0:26.5 (scythe close-up). 0:23.0-0:23.6: dark scythe cross-fades in; gold glints run along the blade edge from the heel to the tip

phases.name: release
phases.what: 0:23.6-0:24.0: a long flame ribbon unrolls along the blade, orange-pink, with a bright pink star at the blade tip; the head collar lights gold

phases.name: impact
phases.what: not shown (idle): on a swing the ribbon becomes the arc trail and the tip star leads it

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: 0:24.0-0:26.5 loop: ribbon ripples back along the blade, dark drips fall from the head, small gold sparkles on collar and pommel

layers.motion: ribbon follows the blade curve and extends 30% past the tip; UV scrolls toward the tip; alpha erosion breaks the trailing edge into strands
layers.notes: the ribbon has several thinner parallel strands inside it (hair-like), which gives it a silky look rather than a flat band

layers.motion: pink four-point star glint at the blade tip, scale twinkle 0.8-1.2
layers.notes: marks the cutting point; on a swing it leads the arc

layers.motion: glints run along the blade edge heel -> tip in 0.5 s
layers.notes: a travelling glint is the cheapest way to say 'this edge just powered up'

layers.motion: few dark drips falling from the blade head, gravity 3, life 0.6 s
layers.notes: dark normal-blended drips give weight under the additive ribbon

layers.motion: small gold glow on the collar where blade meets shaft
layers.notes: anchors the ribbon root

whyItLooksGood: The trail exists on the idle weapon already, so a swing only has to stretch it: idle look and swing look match
Multi-strand ribbon (fine parallel strands with eroded ends) looks like silk or hair, far richer than one solid band
Warm-to-pink gradient along the ribbon length shows direction: hot at the blade, cooler pink at the tail
buildNotes: Video 0:23.0-0:26.5. Build the swing as a trail-ribbon mesh sampled from the blade tip and heel each frame (two-point ribbon), with a shader that multiplies a strand texture (5-7 thin bright lines across the width) by a scrolling noise and an alpha-erosion threshold rising with age. Colour by age: #ffe0b0 at the blade, #e04a8a mid, #40102a tail. Lead with a pink star sprite at the tip. On hit: small pink-gold filament flower at the target, gold petal Emitter, light camera shake. Exaggerate ribbon length (1.3x arc) and strand contrast.

source.title: Zedkiel, Spiderlily weapon VFX set (user reference video)

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: 0:31.0-0:33.75: loop; pink cross-flare pulses, wing tongues flicker, petals stop

layers.motion: flat grey page with dark brush calligraphy, appears in 0.1 s
layers.notes: normal-blended textured surface under the glow: gives the gold something to burn on and keeps contrast

layers.motion: gold stamen burst in the page centre, scale 0.3 -> 1 over 0.6 s
layers.notes: set icon repeated

layers.motion: three curved flame horns per side, stacked vertically, curling upward and outward; later spread into 8-10 tongues per side as wing-fans
layers.notes: symmetric pairs read as wings; stacking three per side gives rhythm

layers.motion: wide soft magenta haze, opacity 0 -> 0.6 over 0.5 s
layers.notes: fills the space between the wings

layers.motion: pink-white cross flare (vertical + horizontal streak) on the spine, flash 3 frames then 1 Hz pulse
layers.notes: cross-shaped flare reads as a sigil on the book

layers.notes: only during the ignition

whyItLooksGood: A normal-blended grey page with black brush strokes sits behind the additive gold: textured, readable, never washes out
Wings made of stacked flame horns are symmetric and iconic; the eye reads 'winged book' instantly
The cross flare on the closed cover gives the second variant its own hero point, distinct from the open-page burst
buildNotes: Video 0:26.5-0:33.75. Self buff: a floating book mesh (or two planes) in front of the caster. Page: plane with a canvas-drawn calligraphy texture, normal blending. Gold burst: additive strand mesh, scale tween. Wings: 3 -> 9 ribbon meshes per side, mirrored, alpha-erosion flame shader, gradient orange root -> pink tip, flicker by re-seeding the noise offset every 3 frames. Cross flare: two thin additive quads crossed, pulse. Gold petal Emitter only in the first 0.8 s. Exaggerate the wing span (2.5x book width).

name: Spider-lily fans and hairpins: paired ornaments ignite into fanned flame bursts and lily tufts

source.title: Zedkiel, Spiderlily weapon VFX set (user reference video)

phases.name: impact

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: loop: pink haze, small dark smoke puffs rising from the fan tops, tufts flicker

layers.motion: one flame tongue per fan rib, radial half-circle, length grows 0 -> 0.5 m in 0.4 s
layers.notes: radial fan of tongues mirrors the fan's own structure

layers.motion: white-gold point at each pivot / tuft, pop over 0.1 s
layers.notes: several small equal cores in a row read as a set

layers.motion: one long horizontal streak through all four tufts, holds at 50%
layers.notes: a shared streak visually links separate objects into one effect

buildNotes: Video 0:33.75-0:41. As a self buff or a multi-point cast: spawn 2-4 small anchors around the caster. Each gets a radial ring of short flame ribbons (alpha-erosion shader) that grow out in 0.4 s, a GlowSphere core pop and a petal Emitter. Draw one thin additive horizontal quad through all anchors at impact. Dark smoke: small normal-blended Emitter, drag 1, gravity -0.5. Exaggerate the shared streak.

name: Toon meteor slam: shadow telegraph, dark rock with fire edge, strobing starburst flash, red puff ball with black swirl rings

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:15.9-0:18.3 (cleanest single hit; same move at 0:00.2-0:02.4 and 0:20.4-0:22.0). A soft dark rock-shaped shadow decal slides across the ground toward the impact point and grows

phases.name: release
phases.what: 0:16.5-0:16.9: a large dark faceted rock with fire only on its leading edge and flame streaks behind it crosses the frame diagonally in about 4 frames

phases.name: impact
phases.what: 0:16.9-0:17.3: three alternating frames of full-screen yellow-white starburst flash and normal frames (strobe), orange fire bursting under the rock, a crescent of orange arcs and a thin magenta line streak

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: 0:17.3-0:18.3: a clump of round red cartoon puff balls with black crescent rings swirling around them, dark smoke wedges, red sparks; it shrinks and darkens and is fully gone ~0.8 s after the hit

layers.motion: rock-silhouette shadow slides along the meteor path toward the impact point, scale 0.6 -> 1.2, opacity 0.3 -> 0.7
layers.notes: the shadow IS the telegraph: it tells you where and when without any glowing UI

layers.motion: big low-poly dark rock, diagonal fall at very high speed (crosses the screen in ~0.25 s), slow tumble
layers.notes: dark, normal-blended rock reads against both sky and fire

layers.motion: flame streaks only on the leading edge and behind, jagged black spike shards mixed in
layers.notes: fire on the front edge only shows the direction of travel

layers.motion: full-screen spiky starburst shape, on-off-on-off-on at 12 fps for 0.4 s
layers.notes: strobing the flash 3 times reads as a much bigger hit than one long flash

layers.motion: flat orange crescent arcs around the impact, fast expand 0 -> 4 m in 0.1 s
layers.notes: partial arcs rather than a full ring look hand-drawn

layers.motion: one thin straight magenta line streak across the impact for 2 frames
layers.notes: a complementary accent line on a red-orange hit

layers.motion: 6-10 round puff balls clustered on the impact, scale up 0.5 -> 1.4 m, then darken and shrink; life 0.6-0.8 s
layers.notes: opaque RED smoke balls (not grey) keep the hit colourful after the flash

layers.motion: 2-3 black crescent rings swirl around the puff cluster, rotating fast, expand and thin out
layers.notes: black swirls are the dark contrast element of the aftermath

layers.motion: thin black shards and red sparks fly outward, gravity 10
layers.notes: small and fast, gone in 0.5 s

layers.motion: heavy 0.3 s
layers.notes: starts on the first flash frame

whyItLooksGood: Shadow telegraph: a moving, growing ground shadow is a diegetic warning and builds tension better than a ring
The rock is on screen only ~4 frames; its speed is sold by the long flame streak, and the hit is sold by the strobe
Strobing flash (flash / normal / flash) makes the impact feel huge without one long white-out
Aftermath is red puffs + black rings, not grey smoke: colour stays saturated and the dark rings carry the swirl motion
Fully clean less than a second after the hit, so repeated casts never clutter
buildNotes: Video 0:15.9-0:18.3. Target the ground point. 0-0.55 s: dark normal-blended decal (rock silhouette texture) sliding along the incoming direction toward the point while scaling up. 0.55 s: spawn a dark low-poly icosahedron rock 25 m up and back, tween to the point in 0.35 s ease-in, with additive flame trail-ribbon and a few black spike sprites. Impact: FinishPass impact flash pulsed 3 times (on 2 frames, off 2 frames), additive spiky starburst sprite 6 m, 2-3 orange arc segments (createRing with partial theta) expanding fast, one thin magenta line for 2 frames, heavy camera shake. Aftermath: instanced normal-blended red spheres/billboards (puffs) with scale-up then darken to #3a0a0a and shrink; 2-3 black ring segments rotating 720 deg/s while expanding; debris Emitter gravity 10. Exaggerate the strobe and the rock speed.

name: Toon meteor volley: three staggered small meteors, each with its own ring, flash and red puff

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:07.5-0:10.0. Several shadow decals appear in a row on the ground, then a burst of flame streaks enters from the top of the frame

phases.name: release
phases.what: 0:08.0-0:08.4: three small rocks, each with a thin white-pink ring around it and fire on the leading edge, fall in a staggered line

phases.name: impact
phases.what: 0:08.4-0:09.3: hits land one after another ~0.25 s apart: each a starburst flash, a black spike crown and a ring pop, the last one biggest

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: 0:09.3-0:10.0: red puff balls at each crater shrink and darken, one at a time in the same order

layers.motion: one shadow per target, slide in and grow
layers.notes: each target gets its own warning

layers.motion: three small dark rocks, 0.25 s apart, diagonal fall
layers.notes: smaller than the single-slam rock so the volley reads as 'many little ones'

layers.motion: thin ring around each falling rock, camera-facing, slight pulse
layers.notes: rings make small rocks readable at a distance

layers.motion: spiky starburst per hit, 3 frames
layers.notes: local flashes, not full-screen, so three of them don't white out the screen

layers.motion: crown of black spike shards per hit, shoot up and out 2 m, life 0.3 s
layers.notes: black spikes are the readable silhouette of each hit

layers.motion: small red puff cluster per crater, darken and shrink
layers.notes: same red-puff signature as the single slam

layers.motion: light per hit, medium on the last
layers.notes: escalation

whyItLooksGood: Staggered hits 0.25 s apart give a drum-roll rhythm; the last one is biggest
Each small rock gets a thin ring so it reads at small size
Local starbursts instead of full-screen flashes keep three hits readable
buildNotes: Video 0:07.5-0:10.0. Pick up to 3-4 enemies; for each, delay 0.25 s * index. Per target: shadow decal slide-in, small rock mesh falling in 0.3 s with additive flame trail and a camera-facing createRing, impact with a local starburst sprite + GlowSphere pop, black spike debris (instanced cones, gravity 12), red puff cluster. Scale the last hit 1.4x and give it medium shake. Exaggerate the black spikes.

name: Monochrome swipe slash: white smoke crescents, ghost arcs that linger, sepia impact frame

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:02.0-0:03.5 (repeats at 0:05.5-0:07.0). 0:02.0-0:02.3: character crouches, a small white glint on the hand

phases.name: release
phases.what: 0:02.3-0:02.45: a big white smoke burst with a sweeping crescent slash and dark motion-streak lines; the screen goes bright

phases.name: impact
phases.what: 0:02.45-0:02.9: a swirl of white wind wraps the target, then a tall vertical translucent crescent lingers for 0.4 s; at 0:02.9 one frame inverts to a pink-white blowout with a black silhouette, then one sepia-graded frame

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: 0:03.0-0:03.5: target knocked back; grey smoke wisps, white pop dots and small dark chunks drift; screen back to normal

layers.motion: big soft white burst at the contact point, 2 frames
layers.notes: white on a dark blue scene is the whole colour story

layers.motion: wide crescent smoke slash, soft feathered edges, alpha erodes over 0.4 s while drifting in the swing direction
layers.notes: the slash is SMOKE, not a hard additive blade: soft, grey-white, semi-opaque

layers.motion: wind swirl wrapping the target (2-3 curved wisps orbiting once), life 0.4 s
layers.notes: wrap-around motion shows the slash connected

layers.motion: tall vertical ghost crescent at 25% opacity, holds 0.4 s, then fades
layers.notes: the lingering ghost arc lets the eye replay the swing

layers.motion: frame 1: near-white blowout with pink tint and the target as a black silhouette; frame 2: sepia/brown full-screen grade; then normal
layers.notes: a warm sepia grade frame is a softer variant of the impact frame than a full value inversion

layers.motion: a few round white pop dots, scale up then vanish, life 0.25 s
layers.notes: simple circle pops add sparkle without colour

layers.motion: small dark chunks kicked out low, gravity 12
layers.notes: dark specks against the white smoke

layers.motion: medium 0.2 s
layers.notes: on the silhouette frame

whyItLooksGood: Zero hue: the effect is pure value (white, greys, black) on a dark blue scene, so it never clashes and always reads
The slash is soft smoke that lingers as a ghost arc, which reads as speed and wind instead of a laser blade
Impact frame by grade: one silhouette blowout frame plus one sepia frame. It punctuates the hit but is gentler than a black/white inversion
Tiny white circle pops and dark chunks give two scales of detail after the hit
buildNotes: Video 0:02.0-0:03.5. Swing: a crescent ribbon mesh (createRing with a partial theta, or custom arc) with a soft smoke texture and alpha-erosion shader, normal blending, grey-white; spawn at the caster facing the target, drift 1 m in the swing direction, erode over 0.4 s. Contact: additive white GlowSphere 2 frames; 2-3 curved wisp ribbons orbiting the target once. Ghost: a tall vertical crescent at 25% opacity, holds 0.4 s. Impact frame: FinishPass flash 1 frame near-white with the target forced black (or simply white flash), then a 1-frame sepia multiply (#c9a98a) grade. Pops: Emitter of white circles scale 0 -> 1 -> 0 in 0.25 s. Exaggerate the crescent width and the ghost-arc hold.

name: Monochrome launch and slam: wind-spiral uppercut, downward smash, dark ground plates tilt up

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:11.0-0:14.0 (repeat at 0:15.75-0:18.0). 0:11.0-0:11.25: caster grabs the target, short pause

phases.name: release
phases.what: 0:11.25-0:12.0: white burst blasts the target upward; a flat white wind spiral (2-3 crescent bands) wraps around the target as it rises, dust ring on the ground

phases.name: impact
phases.what: 0:12.0-0:12.6: caster smashes the target down: white spiky burst with vertical speed lines, one pink-sepia blowout frame with black silhouettes, a white ground ring expands

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: 0:12.6-0:14.0: large dark triangular ground plates tilt up in a ring around the crater, small dark rubble bounces, plates sink back and vanish

layers.motion: white burst on the launch, 2 frames, big
layers.notes: the launch itself already gets a bright beat

layers.motion: 2-3 flat horizontal crescent bands spiralling around the rising target, rising with it, erode over 0.6 s
layers.notes: a wind tornado drawn with three bands instead of hundreds of particles

layers.motion: low dust ring at the launch spot, drag 2
layers.notes: grounds the launch

layers.motion: vertical speed lines and white spikes radiating from the slam point for 3 frames
layers.notes: speed lines aligned with the slam direction

layers.motion: one pink-white blowout frame with black silhouettes, one sepia frame
layers.notes: same impact-frame language as the slash

layers.motion: flat ground ring 0 -> 6 m in 0.15 s, thin, fades 0.3 s
layers.notes: crisp, flat on the ground

layers.motion: 6-8 large flat triangular plates around the crater tilt up 30-50 deg in 0.1 s, hold 0.8 s, sink 0.4 s
layers.notes: a few big dark plates read much better than many small rocks

layers.motion: small rubble cubes bounce outward, gravity 15
layers.notes: secondary scale of debris

layers.motion: heavy 0.35 s
layers.notes: on the slam, not the launch

whyItLooksGood: Two beats with clear weight difference: launch (bright, no shake) and slam (bright + impact frame + heavy shake)
The rising spiral is just 2-3 flat crescent bands: graphic and readable
Big flat ground plates tilt up around the crater: a strong silhouette that says 'the floor broke' and cleans up by sinking
buildNotes: Video 0:11.0-0:14.0. Target an enemy. Launch: GlowSphere white flash, 2-3 createRing partial arcs (normal blended, soft smoke texture) parented to a rising pivot that follows the target up 3 m while rotating 540 deg/s; dust Emitter at feet. buildNotes: Video 0:21.3-0:22.9. Enemy target. 0-0.1 s: one createRing partial arc around the caster, additive. 0.1 s: FinishPass flash tinted #c9a080 for 1 frame, then 2 frames of desaturation if available (else dim). whyItLooksGood: Telegraph is a glyph of the element (a rising half-sun) that collapses right before the strike: anticipation and theme in one shape
A cool blue-white star at the base of a warm fire pillar gives temperature contrast at the exact impact point
Rings travel up the pillar after the hit, so the pillar keeps moving instead of just fading
The crater is a flower of flat molten petals with dark wedges between them: strong radial silhouette with built-in dark/bright contrast

buildNotes: Video 0:00-0:02.75. Ground target. Glyph: an upright additive plane with a canvas half-sun (semicircle, 12 rays, horizon line), scale 3 -> 0.8 m in 0.08 s, then hide for 0.1 s. Pillar: LightPillar 0.6 m wide with a flicker shader, width tween 1 -> 0.2 over 1.5 s. Base flare: four-point star sprite tinted #b8d4ff, plus two smaller violet stars offset +/-1.2 m. Rings: 3 createRing horizontal rings at the pillar, tween y 1 -> 5 m and opacity to 0 over 0.5 s, staggered 0.1 s. Ground: 8-10 petal-shaped additive decals radially, colour tween #fff0a0 -> #c03a00 -> 0 over 1.5 s; between them instanced dark wedge meshes tilted 30 deg, fade last. Falling streaks: Emitter of stretched red sprites with gravity 10. Medium shake + FinishPass impact flash 2 frames. Exaggerate the star flare and the ring climb.

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:00.0-0:04.5. 0:00-0:01.9: near-black frame, thick navy fog; unseen lightning flashes light the fog from above in irregular pulses (0:00.3, 0:01.1-0:01.6), each lighting the fog bank from inside

phases.name: release
phases.what: 0:01.9-0:02.75: a figure walks out of the fog, backlit; it raises an arm, the sky behind brightens to pale blue-white

phases.name: impact
phases.what: 0:02.75-0:03.9: 3-4 large branching bolts strike across the background at once, then flicker and dim slowly over ~1 s; a cluster of small white arcs crackles around the raised hand

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: 0:03.9-0:04.5: background bolts gone, camera cuts close to the hand: bright knotted arcs wrap the fingers and wrist

layers.motion: large slow fog sheets at ground level and behind the caster, drift 0.2 m/s, very long life
layers.notes: fog is the screen the lightning lights up; without it the flashes have nothing to reveal

layers.motion: irregular flashes from above (2-3 per second, random 1-3 frame bursts), light the fog top
layers.notes: lightning you don't see, only its light: pure anticipation

layers.motion: 3-4 big branching bolts across the background, on at full brightness 2 frames, then hold and dim over 1 s with flicker
layers.notes: thick, many-branched, with a soft blue glow around a white core; slow dimming feels cinematic

layers.motion: small knotted arcs around the hand, re-randomised every 2 frames, radius 0.3 m
layers.notes: the second, smaller scale of the same element marks the caster as the source

layers.motion: soft hand glow, opacity flickers with the arcs
layers.notes: lights the arm and fog near the hand

layers.motion: exposure lift 2 frames on the bolt strike, then recover over 0.4 s
layers.notes: camera-style exposure response rather than a white card

whyItLooksGood: Lighting before lightning: the first two seconds only show flashes inside the fog, which builds dread without any bolt
Monochrome blue: everything is navy, pale blue and white, so the brightest white bolt is the only accent
Two scales of the same element: huge sky bolts and tiny hand arcs, linking the storm to the caster
Bolts dim slowly with flicker instead of vanishing, which reads as a real, heavy discharge
buildNotes: Video 0:00-0:04.5. Self channel. Darken the scene (lower ambient, add navy fog colour). Fog: a few large normal-blended smoke billboards with low opacity and slow drift around the caster. Sky flashes: a point/directional light above and the FinishPass flash at 10-20% with random 1-3 frame pulses for 1.9 s. Then 3-4 big lightning-arc polylines (jagged, 2 branch levels) behind the caster, 2 frames full, then opacity 1 -> 0 over 1 s with random frame drops. Hand: small arcs re-randomised every 2 frames + flickering GlowSphere. Exaggerate the darkness first, then the bolt brightness.

buildNotes: Video 0:04.5-0:07.1. Enemy target (chain-capable). Hand arcs: lightning-arc polylines re-randomised every 2 frames. Release: FinishPass flash 1 frame. Bolts: 4-6 jagged ribbon meshes from the caster's shoulder via the hand to the target; give each a width class (1 / 0.4 / 0.1) and its own redraw interval (2, 3, 4 frames); additive white core with blue edge. Fade after 0.85 s with random frame drops. Ground climb: arcs from ground points to the chest, drawn progressively (reveal by length over 0.6 s). buildNotes: Video 0:07.1-0:16.2. For our arena (enemies, ground point under the caster): 0-1 s: lift the caster 2 m, 2-3 lightning-arcs to the ground, then ground-crawl arcs radiating along the floor to each enemy; FinishPass flash 1-2 frames + heavy shake. 1-2.25 s: fan of 30-60 thin jagged ribbons from the origin spreading to the enemies and beyond (instanced line segments re-randomised every 2-4 frames). 2.25 s: four-point starburst with streak rays, second flash; a horizontal LightPillar (rotated 90 deg) through the enemy line. 2.9-9 s: slow-motion feel by slowing all redraw intervals 3x and spawning 10-20 instanced dark flat rock plates floating up slowly (rim-lit blue via a fresnel term), bolts fading over 5 s. Shorten the aftermath to 3 s for gameplay. Exaggerate bolt count; keep the rocks very dark.
